{{Short description|American acoustical engineer (1929–2019)}}
'''Richard H. Lyon''' (August 24, 1929 – January 21, 2019) was an American acoustical engineer.

==Early life==
Lyon was born in [[Evansville, Indiana]], on August 24, 1929, to parents Chester and Gertrude Lyon.<ref name="obit">{{cite news |last1=O'Leary |first1=Mary Beth |title=Richard "Dick" Lyon, acoustics expert and professor emeritus of mechanical engineering, dies at 89 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2019/richard-dick-lyon-acoustics-expert-professor-emeritus-mechanical-engineering-dies-0124 |accessdate=January 26, 2019 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=January 24, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite interview|url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/24720 |last=Lyon |first=Richard H. |subject-link=Richard H. Lyon |interviewer=Robert Fricke |title=Richard Lyon |work= |publisher=American Institute of Physics |location= |date=July 26, 2001}}</ref> 

He attended [[Evansville College]] in his hometown, graduating in 1952 with a bachelor's degree in physics. Lyon pursued further study in the subject at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Upon earning his doctorate in 1955, Lyon joined the faculty of the [[University of Minnesota]], where he was assistant professor of electrical engineering.<ref name="obit" />

==Career==
After three years of teaching, Lyon went to the [[University of Manchester]] for post doctoral study funded by the [[National Science Foundation]]. Lyon then worked at [[Bolt, Beranek, and Newman]] for ten years. He joined MIT faculty as a lecturer in 1963, and was made professor of mechanical engineering in 1970. While teaching, Lyon founded Cambridge Collaborative, Inc. and RH Lyon Corp.<ref name="obit"/> Lyon was elected to membership of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] "for development of statistical energy analysis and machinery diagnostic techniques" in 1995,<ref>{{cite news |title=Richard H. Lyon |url=https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/MemberDirectory/30076.aspx |accessdate=January 26, 2019 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref> the same year he ended his career in academia and won the [[Rayleigh Medal]].<ref name="obit"/> 

He was elected to fellowship of the [[Acoustical Society of America]] and has received the [[ASA Silver Medal|ASA Silver]] (1998) and [[ASA Gold Medal|Gold Medals]] (2003), as well as the Gold Medal from the Acoustical Society of India.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Unger |first1=Gladys L. |last2=Wood |first2=Eric W. |title=Richard H. Lyon – Sounds of Quality Products |url=http://www.sandv.com/downloads/1606unga.pdf |accessdate=January 26, 2019 |work=Sound and Vibration |date=June 2016}}</ref> 

==Death==
Lyon died on January 21, 2019, aged 89.<ref name="obit"/> He is survived by his wife, Jean Lyon, and his three children, [[Kathy Davis]], Geoffrey Lyon, and Suzanne (Sue) Lyon Riggle.
